subject: Storage preservation policies and tenant routing: clarify asks & next steps
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@acme-corp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: LegalOps <contracts@acme-corp.com>, Darren Mills <darren.mills@cloudops.acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: per-tenant preservation windows + regional routing options

Hi Jonas,

Quick follow from our security review: Acme needs two pieces to be configurable per-tenant before we can move to procurement: (1) a per-tenant preservation window (how long soft-deleted data is recoverable before final erase) and (2) a priority routing policy so tenant data can be pinned to a preferred storage region (with automatic fallbacks).

Questions we have:
- Is the preservation window adjustable via API or only admin console?
- Can we set a legal-hold override that prevents purge even if TTL expires?
- When a tenant is pinned to a region, can we guarantee new writes and backups stay in-zone (and what are the fallback behaviours during capacity constraints)?
- Any cost/latency impact guidance for 30d vs 90d vs 365d preservation buckets?

Can you loop in engineering and product for a short doc we can use in our SOW? We referenced your retention matrix draft in the call but need specifics for our security team.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Li
Head of Cloud Security, Acme Corp

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Emma Li <emma.li@acme-corp.com>, LegalOps <contracts@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: per-tenant preservation windows + regional routing options

Hi all — forwarding Emma's ask here. TL;DR: Acme wants per-tenant preservation TTLs, an admin/API toggle for legal hold, and a routing priority that pins tenant writes to a region with defined fallback rules.

Karthik / Lauren — can you confirm technical constraints and propose an implementation approach + minimal policy surface (API fields, admin UI, and audit events) we can commit to in the SOW? Please include:
- API contract sketch (PUT /tenants/{id}/retention + routing flags)
- Legal hold semantics (who can set/unset, audit log format, retention override duration)
- Storage routing policy (preferred_region, failover_regions, emergency-fail-open vs deny-write behaviour)
- Expected cost delta for common preservation buckets (30d/90d/365d) and an ops note about long-tail cold storage copies
- A rough timeline (design -> staging -> GA) and any risks to SLA.

Emma — I'll keep you in the loop; if LegalOps wants to propose exact contract language we can slot that into the SOW draft.

Jonas
VP, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Emma Li <emma.li@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Jun 2028 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: per-tenant preservation windows + regional routing options

Jonas / Lauren / Emma — wrote up a short technical response and a proposed minimal feature set. Attaching a retention matrix and a draft routing spec for review. High-level answers first:

1) Preservation window: implementable both via admin console and the tenant API. Proposal: a tenant-level "preservation_days" integer (0, 7, 30, 90, 365, 1095) and a per-resource soft-delete flag. Default: 30 days.

2) Legal hold override: yes. A legal_hold object that marks resources as exempt from purge until explicit release. Only accounts with "legal_admin" role can set/unset; every change emits an immutable audit event stored in the control plane.

3) Regional pinning & failover: we can add a "preferred_region" field plus an ordered "fallback_regions" list. Behaviour options:
- failover-mode: redirect-writes (writes go to fallback region, metadata indicates migration-in-progress)
- failover-mode: deny-writes (reject writes if preferred region unavailable)

We recommend "redirect-writes" by default with a configurable timeout for cross-region writes before we mark the tenant as multi-region for replication purposes. This keeps apps online but increases egress/cross-region cost.

4) Cost/latency: rough delta estimates (ballpark for planning):
- 30d default: baseline
- 90d: +8-12% storage cost, negligible steady-state latency impact
- 365d: +30-40% storage cost, slightly higher backup windows
Legal_hold: negligible direct cost but increases retention tail and complexity of deletions.

Risks and notes:
- Admin/UI: exposing legal_hold controls must include approval flows to reduce accidental releases.
- Compliance: need a clear delete-authorization audit trail to satisfy auditors (we'll emit an event per purge action).
- Migration: pinning existing tenants to regions may require data rehydration/copy windows (coordination with infra).

Proposed timeline (alpha to customer pilot):
- 2 weeks: API/contract design & spec, include sample requests/responses
- 4 weeks: storage routing implementation + simple admin UI
- 2 weeks: staging rollout, create a tenant-scoped feature flag
- 2 weeks: pilot with Acme (monitoring + cost telemetry)

I'll attach Retention_Matrix_v3.xlsx and the routing draft in a follow-up. Feedback welcome.

-Karthik
Senior Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Emma Li <emma.li@acme-corp.com>

Date: Wed, 19 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: per-tenant preservation windows + regional routing options

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our side:
- We prefer "deny-writes" for our HIPAA-controlled namespaces unless you can provide guaranteed encryption-in-transit assurances during cross-region write redirects. If redirect is used, can Redwood provide per-write provenance metadata?
- For legal hold, LegalOps wants an opinionated release/approval workflow. Can Redwood expose webhook hooks so we can wire into our internal approval system?
- Pilot timeline request: can you aim to have a staging tenant configured by July 8? That gives our team two weeks to exercise erasure tests before SOW sign-off.

If you can produce a short SOW appendix describing these behaviours and a one-page cost projection (30/90/365) for our expected data volume (estimated 12TB active + 18TB backups), we can accelerate procurement.

Emma

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

- Karthik: lock down API contract + provide sample requests that include per-write provenance headers and an example webhooks schema (due: 2028-06-24). Attach draft SOW appendix.
- Lauren: produce a one-page cost projection for 12TB active / 18TB backup across 30/90/365 windows and call out cross-region egress assumptions (due: 2028-06-25).
- Marissa: coord with infra to reserve a staged tenant in eu-west-1 for Acme pilot and enable the tenant feature flag (due: 2028-07-06).
- Jonas (me): consolidate SOW appendix and coordinate LegalOps language for approval flows; circulate to Emma by 2028-06-28.

Emma — we'll aim to have a staging tenant available by July 8 as requested; Marissa will confirm the exact time once infra reservation is done. Expect a short SOW appendix and cost page in the next week.

Jonas
